assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turns a biological process, regulated protein degradation by the ubiquitin-proteasome system, into a defined chemical design principle: bifunctional molecules and molecular glues that rewire E3 ligases. Original concept, clear mechanism, a general tool for biologists, and drugs now in clinical use. Strong medical relevance.
assessment.attribution: PROTAC concept and first demonstrations trace to Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto and Kim); Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains molecular glues; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structural work. Crews, Deshaies and Handa is a coherent trio, but dividing credit between the PROTAC and glue branches is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups across industry and academia, with multiple degraders in late-stage clinical trials. The field is still young on clinical outcomes, but the chemistry is firmly established and recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue branches should be recognised together or separately.
Clinical efficacy is not yet fully established; I have not verified the latest trial results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing, built on reversible-terminator and related sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, changed all of biology and medicine, including my own field of genome stability, where mutation spectra are now read directly. Impact is enormous and lasting; the chemical core is nucleotide chemistry on a surface.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman made the Solexa sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and single-molecule approach; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing platform was the first commercial parallel system. Ju and Mayer have credible claims, so the prize configuration is contested.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and independently validated at global scale for roughly two decades. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Platform history involves several parallel technologies and patent disputes, so credit is hard to split in three.
Whether the committee views it as chemistry rather than biology or medicine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale mass-spectrometry proteomics turned protein measurement into a routine analytical chemistry, which I value as someone who trusts measured quantities over assumptions. Broad and lasting impact across biochemistry and medicine.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, SILAC-based quantitative proteomics), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH proteomics, ICAT) and Yates (shotgun and database searching) have distinct, decisive contributions. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also have strong claims, so the three-person cut is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature and reproduced across thousands of laboratories. Part of the field was already recognised by the 2002 prize for ionisation methods, which may count against it.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for biomolecular mass spectrometry.
Choosing three among at least six strong contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors are engineered chemical-biology tools that perform specific deaminase chemistry on DNA to change a single base without double-strand breaks. Very original, general and quickly adopted, with clinical trials under way. The chemistry is cytidine and adenosine deamination, which I know well from nucleotide metabolism.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader. Komor (cytosine base editor) and Gaudelli (adenine base editor, including the evolved TadA deaminase) were the lead authors. Kondo and Nishida independently developed a related cytidine deaminase editor, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and in the clinic, but the field is only about ten years old and long-term safety, such as off-target deamination, is still being worked out. Recognition could be considered slightly early.
uncertainties: Off-target and bystander editing may affect how stable the long-term assessment is.
Whether the committee prefers to pair this with CRISPR, which was recognised in 2020.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase and tRNA pairs lets biologists install non-natural amino acids in living cells. This is a clear chemical solution to a biological constraint and a general tool, with many applications in mechanistic enzymology, including radical enzymes such as RNR.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first orthogonal pairs in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended the method to eukaryotes and multicellular organisms, and to quadruplet codons and ribosome engineering. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed, so the distribution of credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced over about twenty years and widely used as a standard tool. Recognition is mature. Impact on medicine is growing through protein therapeutics.
uncertainties: Whether the main credit belongs to the original orthogonal-pair concept or to later extensions.
Overlap with the 2018 prize for directed evolution and the Nobel recognition of related tools is limited but not zero.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase carries out one of the most important and difficult reactions in biology, N2 reduction, with a unique metal cofactor. Structural and mechanistic work links atomic structure to catalysis, which fits my preference for chemical mechanism under a biological process. Importance is very high, but the full mechanism is still incomplete.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures and FeMo cofactor features, including the central carbide; Einsle contributed high-resolution structures; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanism and genetics; Ribbe contributed cofactor biosynthesis. The credit is spread over many people and the ideal trio is unclear.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well confirmed independently. The catalytic mechanism and substrate binding are still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable and recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: The detailed catalytic cycle and substrate binding site are not fully resolved.
Credit is dispersed across structure, mechanism and biosynthesis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery that m6A in mRNA is a reversible modification with writers, erasers and readers created an epitranscriptomic regulatory layer, with chemical identity of the mark and a defined demethylation reaction. Significant for gene regulation, cancer and development. From a nucleotide-chemistry viewpoint it is appealing but I would want the quantitative evidence to be solid.
assessment.attribution: He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and framed the reversible-modification concept; Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini and Meyer) developed transcriptome-wide mapping. Jia and Yang also contributed to FTO and m6A work. Credit is split among several groups and mapping methods.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated at the level of the writer and reader machinery, but there are real disputes about FTO substrate specificity (m6A versus m6Am), mapping resolution and the physiological roles of some marks. The interpretation is not yet fully stable.
uncertainties: Disputes over FTO substrate specificity and the accuracy of antibody-based mapping.
Many downstream functional claims depend on indirect evidence that I have not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules electrically through nanopores combines protein engineering, analytical chemistry and a practical sequencing technology that detects base modifications directly. Original idea with real practical impact, including direct detection of modified nucleotides.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton and Deamer demonstrated the basic principle; Bayley engineered the alpha-hemolysin pore and chemistry; Akeson showed enzyme-controlled DNA translocation that made sequencing possible. Choosing the best three of five is difficult, and one or more of the early contributors may no longer be living, which I could not verify.
assessment.maturity: The technology is now commercial and independently validated, with accuracy improving. The concept is mature, though accuracy gaps compared with other platforms have only recently narrowed.
uncertainties: Credit split between the principle, the engineered pore and enzyme-controlled motion.
Overlap with the sequencing-by-synthesis candidate if both are considered.
